label: Exceeded god: something divine with being is exceeded in being by a non-divine thing
definition: SomeGodExceededInBeing IsGod InAct MoreIn esse holds when there are g and y such that g is God, g is in act in esse, y is not God, and y is more in esse than g. Ordinary meaning: there is a god, and it is not the highest reality. Example: a divine craftsman who looks to a Form more real than himself. It is not atheism and does not say God lacks being.
note: Analyst framework definition of a rival position; attribution deferred. Motivated by demiurgic and finite-god theologies. Rival of GodIsMaximalInBeing on the same IsGod, InAct, MoreIn and esse. Stronger than the negation: the god has being and what exceeds it is not God. IsGod is the supplied predicate; whether a being so exceeded deserves the name under the nominal definition is the dispute, not something this definition settles.
